levelRule: Level-based games need at least 20 authored levels with level select through env.progress.

records.hashCheck: The reviewer recorded all six hashes at the start and the end of each round; both rounds' records were identical, and the served modules matched in Chrome.

findings.observation: Machine 20's tip said every beam ends level, but two beams must lean right. It now reads 'Two beams lean right, one hangs level: read each lamp'.
Machine 18's tip ('move the right one first') was meaningless and machine 7's tip omitted that moving a placed slider costs two moves. Both were rewritten.

152 rotate prompts on the optimal path named a mass of the same weight as the one already selected, and vertical move prompts named a peg they did not reach. Sliders are now named with their rail, a plain mass is called plain when needed, and vertical steps name only the beam.
Machines 3 and 4 had no budget, so an informed random placer reached 28% at 240 s. They now have optimum + 3; it wins 0 of 60 on each.
An exhausted, unsolved machine was lost 1.2 s after the needles rested, so a 1.5 s reader always lost. A visible 6 s countdown now runs, any undo or reset cancels it, and idle still loses.
Unused options, an unread cap flag, unreachable no-solution advice and stale generator markers were removed.

openNotes: Late machines have 240 to 20,160 complete placements with exactly one solved; since undo refunds moves, a patient exhaustive search can solve them. The reviewer's no-prompt bots (greedy with climbing, 2-ply with restarts, depth 3-5 look-ahead) beat at most 12 of 24 machines and none of 14-24.
Beam A on machine 20 is satisfied in every complete placement, so the machine plays as two gates.
Optimal move counts rise only from 1 to 8; the search size does not rise monotonically.
Machines 1 and 2 are easy by design: random play wins 25 of 100 on machine 1 and mashing 69 and 12 of 100 on machines 1 and 2.
Text fit was checked with a width model, not measured fonts; at 371 px the host header clips the prompt, which stays in full on the canvas.
